sentences.text: Here’s the heart of Rule nineteen.
A vessel that detects another by radar alone shall determine whether a close-quarters situation is developing or risk of collision exists.
If so, she shall take avoiding action in ample time.
If that action is an alteration of course, then so far as possible she shall avoid two things.
First, an alteration of course to port for a vessel forward of the beam, other than a vessel being overtaken.
Second, an alteration of course toward a vessel abeam or abaft the beam.
For a vessel ahead, a substantial turn to starboard is usually the safe choice.
